nodes.claim: A typed claims graph with a criteria-governed evidence ladder is a well-precedented substrate for machine-written theory — the structure is inherited from real prior art; the benefit is a bet this program must measure, not cite.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-08-26 with the claim narrowed to what the evidence licenses; go-9 carries the counter-evidence that forced the narrowing (its edge landed as refines rather than contradicts precisely because this claim conceded the point — go-6 has the typing rule). Structural precedent, each element separately: typed deliberation nodes — IBIS (Kunz & Rittel 1970: topics, issues, questions of fact, positions, arguments and model problems as element types; built for coordinating contested planning, with no evidence ladder and 'settling' as a social act) and gIBIS at tool scale (Conklin & Begeman 1988, typed IBIS networks over a shared database). Contradictions as first-class structure — Dung 1995 makes attack a first-class relation from which acceptance is computable, the formal license for the contradicts edge; SWAN (Ciccarese et al. 2008) was designed to foreground contradictory assertions in community discourse. The closest built precedent is micropublications (Clark, Ciccarese & Goble 2014): claims as nodes, supports and challenges as typed edges, and structural health queries — the model's competency questions include listing assertions unsupported by evidence (body-level content, index-grade; paraphrase, not quotation) — which is this lane's orphan/health practice a decade early; ORKG (Jaradeh et al. 2019) is the at-scale existence proof. The ladder's precedent is GRADE (Guyatt et al. 2008): four ordered levels of evidence quality (the 2008 paper's own term; 'certainty' is later GRADE wording) whose movement is governed by NAMED criteria — the import being that a ladder without named transition criteria is not GRADE-like, which is why §4 defines each rung by the evidence it requires and why go-8's per-source grades matter. One consequence recorded from Dung rather than smoothed over: there, status is DERIVED from the attack graph under a semantics; here it is stamped per node with named criteria. The reconciliation this program runs: the stamped ladder is the GRADE half, and the health instrument's contradiction count (go-5) is the Dung half's seed — a node under an unresolved contradicts edge is challenged regardless of its stamped rung. What remains uncitable is efficacy: the argumentation literature the design-rationale field imported its usefulness claims from had, by 1994, failed to substantiate them (go-9). Progress-as-status-motion stays this program's own wager, measured by its own health numbers.

Clark T, Ciccarese PN, Goble CA 2014, 'Micropublications: a semantic model for claims, evidence, arguments and annotations in biomedical communications', Journal of Biomedical Semantics 5(1):28, DOI 10.1186/2041-1480-5-28, PMC4530550, arXiv:1305.3506. Index-grade, structure abstract-grade

nodes.claim: Accumulating knowledge bases decay measurably; this program measures its graphs on the literature's own health dimensions and treats pruning as first-class — transferring that discipline to machine-written theory graphs is its own, still-unmeasured bet.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-08-26 with the claim restated to what the sources reach: they ground the dimensions and the decay, not a diagnosis of THIS program — no cited corpus is a machine-written claims graph, so the transfer clause is load-bearing, exactly as in go-1. The dimension mapping: staleness→timeliness, near-duplicates→conciseness, contradictions→consistency, orphans→interlinking, four of the 18 quality dimensions (69 metrics) the linked-data quality survey systematized (Zaveri et al. 2016); and 'refinement' — completion PLUS error detection — is half of a named research area, so pruning is first-class in the literature too, not just in this charter (Paulheim 2017). The decay evidence, cross-domain: in Stack Overflow, 58.4% of obsolete answers were probably obsolete when first posted and only 20.5% are ever updated once observed obsolete (Zhang et al. 2021) — rot is often BORN, not aged, so go-5's timestamp-based staleness metric is a lower bound, same epistemic shape as go-6's contradiction count; one in five STM articles (1997–2012 corpus) suffers reference rot, and the companion study found three of four URI references lead to content that has drifted (Klein et al. 2014; Jones et al. 2016) — a cited node's health decays through its links while its text never changes, which is the charter's §11 source-rot rule and go-8's verification-grade labels stated as measured fact; and in maintained software documentation, up-to-dateness and completeness issues are both frequently mentioned in a mined taxonomy of 878 artifacts (Aghajani et al. 2019) — decay and gaps co-dominate; the abstract names no single dominant failure. One caution absorbed from the strongest counter-result: Wikipedia's quality-control tooling measurably crippled the growth it was built to manage (Halfaker et al. 2013) — pruning policy is a system variable with second-order costs, which is why go-5 keeps every metric descriptive and every prune a judged act with a log row, never a gate.
sources: Zaveri A, Rula A, Maurino A, Pietrobon R, Lehmann J, Auer S 2016, 'Quality assessment for Linked Data: A Survey', Semantic Web 7(1):63-93, DOI 10.3233/SW-150175 (online-first 2015; cited by issue). Index-grade; dimension NAMES corroborated multi-index, their grouping into categories deliberately not quoted
Paulheim H 2017, 'Knowledge graph refinement: A survey of approaches and evaluation methods', Semantic Web 8(3):489-508, DOI 10.3233/SW-160218 (online-first 2016). Index-grade

Zhang H, Wang S, Chen T-H, Zou Y, Hassan AE 2021, 'An Empirical Study of Obsolete Answers on Stack Overflow', IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 47(4):850-862, DOI 10.1109/TSE.2019.2906315, arXiv:1903.12282 — 58.4% born-obsolete and 20.5% ever-updated figures abstract-grade

Klein M, Van de Sompel H, Sanderson R, Shankar H, Balakireva L, Zhou K, et al. 2014, 'Scholarly Context Not Found: One in Five Articles Suffers from Reference Rot', PLoS ONE 9(12):e115253, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0115253, PMID 25541969. Index-grade, headline figure abstract-grade

Jones SM, Van de Sompel H, Shankar H, Klein M, Tobin R, Grover C 2016, 'Scholarly Context Adrift: Three out of Four URI References Lead to Changed Content', PLoS ONE 11(12):e0167475, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0167475 — content-drift companion. Index-grade

Aghajani E, Nagy C, Vega-Márquez OL, Linares-Vásquez M, Moreno L, Bavota G, Lanza M 2019, 'Software Documentation Issues Unveiled', ICSE 2019:1199-1210, DOI 10.1109/ICSE.2019.00122 — 878 artifacts mined; up-to-dateness and completeness both frequently mentioned, abstract-grade

nodes.claim: Cross-graph structure is where the combination lives, so global ids and typed cross-edges are load-bearing, not decoration.
nodes.detail: Central's combination theory is largely MADE of cross-graph edges (gen-3 supports cen-1, pat-4 supports cen-2). The optimizer therefore validates cross-references every run (no dangling ids), keeps id prefixes stable forever, and treats a broken cross-edge as a build failure, not a cosmetic one. Refined 2026-09-02 by go-12: resolution is the floor, not the ceiling — the checker holds that a target EXISTS, while whether the edge still warrants against the target's current claim is a currency the health instrument now measures (25 of 321 edges older than their target's claim at first measurement, this node's own go-3→cen-1 among them). Re-read against cen-1's 08-28 rewrite to the hierarchical fork: the support stands — the fork is made of cross-graph edges too, more of them, so the claim here is truer of the rewritten target than of the original.

nodes.claim: Self-optimization is legitimate exactly when it is versioned, total and reversible.
nodes.detail: This lane may change the schema and its own methods — the owner asked for a graph optimizer 'including itself' — under three bounds: every schema change bumps the version and migrates ALL graphs in the same run or does not land; changes are reversible from git history; and the optimizer never rewrites another lane's CONTENT (claims, statuses, details) — only structure (format, merges of literal duplicates with a log row, id hygiene). Content is each lane's; shape is this lane's. Re-read 2026-09-02 against go-1's 08-26 narrowing, flagged by go-12's instrument: the refinement stands — go-1 now claims the structure is precedented and the benefit a bet, and this node bounds how the lane may alter the structure while the bet runs; the bounds are what keep the bet measurable.

nodes.claim: Graph health is a committed measurement instrument — named metrics with named thresholds, computed by a tool in the repo — never a hand count in a summary.
nodes.detail: The first scheduled run replaced hand-counting with graph/health.mjs: per lane, status mix, stale conjectures (untouched >14 days), orphans (program-wide degree zero; the rate is the list over the node count) and detail weight (>400 words flagged); program-wide, unresolved contradicts edges and near-duplicate claim pairs (token Jaccard ≥ 0.5, cross-graph pairs included). Three design choices carry the theory. (a) Thresholds are named constants in the tool, so changing one is a reviewable diff rather than drift in a summary's prose. (b) Orphan degree is program-wide: a node referenced only from another lane's graph is not an orphan, because cross-graph edges are the combination (go-3) — a per-file orphan count would misread exactly the nodes central most depends on. (c) The tool is descriptive, never gating: check.mjs holds form, health.mjs reports signals, and the judgment (merge, prune, flag, ignore) stays with the optimizer — every metric here is a proxy a lane could Goodhart the moment it gates (trivial edges to dodge the orphan count, detail sharded into filler nodes to dodge the budget). Near-duplicate flags in particular are candidates to READ, not to merge: token overlap cannot tell a duplicate from a deliberate cross-lane mirror (bod-2/gen-2), and only literal duplicates are ever merged (§5). First measurement, 2026-08-26: 43 nodes, 59 edges (25 cross-graph), mix 12/22/9/0, zero contradictions, zero near-duplicate pairs, six nodes over detail budget. Interpretation caveat from go-2's evidence: the staleness metric is a timestamp proxy and rot is often born rather than aged (Zhang et al. 2021), so a low stale count is a lower bound on decay, not an all-clear. Additions since, each argued at its own node: 08-28, per-lane graded-sources count — source-string verification markers only, because the '-grade' suffix is homonymous in prose and only a reader can tell a verification label from a domain adjective (go-10); 09-01, run recency — each lane's last LOG.md row date and age, silence flagged past SILENT_DAYS=2 (go-11); 09-02, edge currency — each node's last claim-change date recovered from git and every edge older than its target's claim listed under its owner lane, with prose rung-label drift, same-type mutual pairs and per-lane inbound cross-edges beside it (go-12). That last addition ends the instrument's no-git posture: check.mjs already shells to git for §7's path sets, the branch's only history IS git (SCHEMA: 'history lives in git'), and the tool says plainly when it has none rather than guessing. Still zero packages.

nodes.claim: A zero in the contradiction metric measures recording, not harmony: adversarial findings that die in prose leave the graph looking more agreed than the program is.
nodes.detail: Measured fact, first health pass (2026-08-26): zero contradicts edges across 43 nodes — after three scout runs whose adversarial passes each forced substantive corrections. Within-run corrections rightly vanish into the rewritten claim; the gap is standing, surviving tension: the one genuine cross-lane tension then live (gen-5's LLM analogy against pat-6's cited negative results) was typed refines, indistinguishable from a friendly sharpening, and the count read 0. Consequence for the instrument (go-5): the contradiction count is a lower bound on live disagreement — a tension registers only when some lane elects the strongest edge type. Practice offered, not imposed (content is the lanes', §5): when external evidence cuts against a claim another node STILL asserts, type contradicts and let the target resolve it into a refinement; once the target has narrowed, refines is the honest type (go-9→go-1 is the worked example). A contradicts edge is a work item a later run is forced to see. Exercised end-to-end 2026-08-27→29, with no optimizer involvement: tests elected the program's first contradicts edge in exactly the offered split-verdict shape (tst-6→cen-1, contradicts scoped to the singular cen-1 still asserted, refines for the half it sharpened); central's next run revised cen-1 to the hierarchical fork, naming the edge as what it resolved; the electing lane then retired the contradicts after a clause-by-clause re-read — refines kept, supports added — and re-homed the residual tension at tst-5/tst-8. Two days, election to resolution. New count semantics from that cycle: a reading of 0 is now ambiguous between never-elected and elected-and-resolved; the point-in-time instrument cannot distinguish them (resolution traces live in LOG rows and the nodes' own accounting), so the health summary narrates resolutions rather than reading 0 as concord — go-11 generalizes the blindness to a program that stops recording. The lower-bound caveat stands on every reading. Two further readings, 2026-09-02. Pattern's 09-02 LOG row writes 'pat-4 now contradicts cen-2 at the boundary' as a flag for central — the word, in prose, no edge elected — so the count reads 0 while a lane has written it down; go-12 measures why a LOG-row flag reaches nobody. And the review rubric (09-01) scores an opened contradiction under Innovative and its resolution by revision under Effective — the first incentive pointing against under-recording; whether it produces elected edges or performed ones is the next measurement.

nodes.claim: Detail has a weight budget: past a few hundred words a node is an essay wearing one status, and the fix is fission into nodes the ladder can grip separately.
nodes.detail: One-node-one-status only checks anything while a node carries roughly one claim (go-1): a 700-word detail hides which sentence the status covers and hands the skeptic no target smaller than the whole essay. Fission restores per-claim status at zero information cost; splitting is the owning lane's act, the optimizer flags weight (health.mjs, 400 words) and records the pattern here — a smell threshold, never a gate (go-5's Goodhart argument). The measurement series. 08-26: 6 of 43 over budget (14%), all born cited from scout runs, three hand-labelling sub-claims inline — lanes doing manually what granularity does structurally. 08-28: 23 of 69 (33%; 11% on the like-for-like nine-graph baseline), maximum 1531w (map-6), argument-only nodes crossing too, zero fissions — the flag as published changed no behaviour because no flagged lane's read path surfaced it, so the lever chosen was central, the one lane that reads everything and may append to every QUESTIONS.md. 09-01: the lever worked — five parents fissioned within days of central routing the measurement by name (cen-2→cen-8, gen-5→gen-12/13, tst-5→tst-8, map-6→map-7..10 with an honest cited→argued demotion, pat-3→pat-9..11; go-10 has the channel accounting) — yet the rate rose to 31 of 88 (35%), because every fission left its parent or a child over the line: fission conserves words. 09-02, fourth measurement: 48 of 120 (40%). The three lanes seeded 09-01 are all under budget (maxima 200–241w) — nodes are born light and grow heavy — while established lanes' scouts keep landing the heaviest nodes the program has (tst-1 1271w, a conjecture→argued move; que-3 1195w; gen-14 882w; bod-13 856w); database's row records db-6/db-8/db-9 landing at 410–416w 'after four trims … recorded rather than sharded' — the first lane to state the budget as a trade consciously taken, the discipline working where the number does not move. Verdict, unchanged and sharpened: fission restores statuses the ladder can grip but does not pay the budget; the budget binds at write time or not at all, and the two channels that have enforced it are the in-lane adversarial pass (tst-5) and a lane's own trimming loop (database) — both authoring-time, neither the flag.

nodes.claim: The lanes run a finer evidence scale than the schema knows — per-source verification grades — and if the schema ever absorbs it, it will be as a defined vocabulary: waiting for the emergent convention to settle was measured to be waiting on something the architecture cannot produce.
nodes.detail: Bottom-up observation, three scout runs in: genetic, map and pattern each independently invented per-source verification grading, in three different vocabularies — genetic writes 'abstract-grade' and 'vendor-grade' inline; pattern writes 'abstract/snippet/repo-table-grade' and 'index-grade'; map writes per-node 'Verification grade:' sentences ('full text', 'abstract level') with no suffix convention — and map and genetic additionally mark own-inference sub-claims inline (go-7 has the strings). Same instinct three ways is schema pressure: cited is one rung, but what the lanes actually record is which source cleared which bar, and today that lives in strings where check.mjs cannot hold it (a 'full text' label can silently outlive the verification it names, and nothing forces a grade at all). Candidate schema v2: an optional enumerated grade per source entry, checkable and countable by health.mjs. Why not this run: the vocabulary is one day old and still moving — three lanes, three overlapping but different label sets — and a schema change migrates every graph in the same run or does not land (§5, go-4); that migration is cheap at 43 nodes and grows with the corpus, but an enum frozen too early forces a v3 when the convention settles differently, which doubles exactly the cost the rule exists to bound. Decision rule: revisit after the three unscouted lanes (body, questions, tests) have each run a scout — if the grade vocabulary holds across six lanes it is stable enough to freeze, and the cost curve then says migrate promptly rather than let string-grade sources accumulate. THE RULE FIRED 2026-08-28: all three lanes have scouted, and the vocabulary did not hold — it proliferated and split (census and verdict at go-10, which now carries the decision). No v2 grade enum lands, and the original claim's 'once the convention stops moving' clause is retired as wrong-headed rather than merely premature: the convention was never going to stop moving on its own, because nothing carries one lane's style to another (go-10's mechanism). What survives of this node: the observation that lanes independently want per-source grading was real and still stands — three MORE vocabularies appeared after it was written — and the cost-curve argument (unstructured grade strings accumulate migration debt) transfers intact to go-10's schema-defined path.

nodes.claim: The efficacy of argumentation substrates is unproven, not proven: the argumentation literature design rationale imported its usefulness claims from had failed to substantiate them, and — by this lane's own inference — two of the four documented formalization costs survive a machine author.
nodes.detail: This node exists to keep go-1 honest. The evidence, stated with its own limits. (1) Buckingham Shum & Hammond 1994 examined the two foundational claims of argumentation-based design rationale — that expressing rationale as argumentation is useful, and that designers can use the notations — and found that research into semiformal argumentation OUTSIDE the design context had 'failed to substantiate convincingly either' (their scope qualifier, kept: the imported literature failed to license the claims, which is not the same as the field disconfirming itself); the same abstract also reports emerging indications that argumentation-based rationale CAN assist certain kinds of design reasoning and be useful later — this is a mixed source, cited as one. The sting stands: the same first author later built ScholOnto, a claim-centric scholarly graph (Buckingham Shum et al. 2000) — builder and doubter are one person, the posture this program should copy. (2) Of the four named problems of formal representation (Shipman & Marshall 1999) — cognitive overhead, tacit knowledge, premature structure, situational structure — this lane's own inference, marked as such: the first two largely dissolve for a machine author, which pays the discretization cost without reluctance or interruption, while premature structure and situational structure do not — forcing a nascent idea into claim-plus-status before the right decomposition is known is go-7's essay-node pathology from the other side, and a fixed type/status vocabulary fits some theory domains worse than others. Their prescription, incremental formalization, is partially absorbed by the conjecture rung and go-8's rule against freezing a moving convention. (3) gIBIS's own authors reported the 'rather austere selection of node and link types' made discretizing vague thought unnatural (Conklin & Begeman 1988, snippet-grade). Edge typing, per go-6's own rule: this landed as refines, not contradicts, because go-1 narrowed its claim to concede exactly this point in the same run — had go-1 kept its unconditional 'right substrate' form, this would be the program's first contradicts edge. The open question it leaves is empirical: months of real status motion without padding substantiates the bet locally; stagnation-by-rewording means the critique won, and the digest is where that verdict becomes visible. Re-read 2026-09-02 against go-8's 08-28 restatement, flagged by go-12's instrument: the support stands and sharpens — Shipman & Marshall's incremental formalization argues for the path go-8 kept (a schema-defined grade field, optional and empty at migration): an enum imposed is premature structure, an optional field is incremental.
sources: Buckingham Shum S, Hammond N 1994, 'Argumentation-based design rationale: what use at what cost?', International Journal of Human-Computer Studies 40(4):603-652, DOI 10.1006/ijhc.1994.1029. Index-grade, conclusion abstract-grade

Shipman FM III, Marshall CC 1999, 'Formality Considered Harmful: Experiences, Emerging Themes, and Directions on the Use of Formal Representations in Interactive Systems', Computer Supported Cooperative Work 8(4):333-352, DOI 10.1023/A:1008716330212. Index-grade, four-problem taxonomy abstract-grade

Conklin J, Begeman ML 1988, 'gIBIS: a hypertext tool for exploratory policy discussion', ACM TOIS/TOOIS 6(4):303-331, DOI 10.1145/58566.59297 — cost quotes snippet-grade from a hosted PDF, wording unconfirmed at source

Buckingham Shum S, Motta E, Domingue J 2000, 'ScholOnto: an ontology-based digital library server for research documents and discourse', International Journal on Digital Libraries 3(3):237-248, DOI 10.1007/s007990000034. Index-grade

nodes.claim: Unschematized conventions do not converge across fresh-session lanes — they proliferate and drift into homonymy; convergence happens only through an active channel (an enforced artifact, central's read-path relay, or in-lane adversarial re-derivation), so schema absorption is an act of coordination, never a ratification of emergence.
nodes.detail: Measured 2026-08-28, two days after go-8. Census over nine graphs: 18 distinct '-grade' tokens (16 excluding this lane's meta-prose), from 11 by the same census when go-8 was written; the suffix homonymous — 'record-grade' states how a source was verified, tests' 'instrument-grade model' is a domain adjective (central's 'instrument-grade standard' was deleted in cen-1's 08-28 revision — inline grade strings rot, as go-2 predicts); placement split four ways (two source-string syntaxes, pattern in detail prose, map in free-form sentences); newly scouted lanes adopted none. Mechanism, this lane's inference: a run is a fresh session reading the charter, the schema and its own files, so propagation follows the RECEIVING lane's read path — 'instrument-grade' crossed lanes via central's append to tests' QUESTIONS.md, while genetic's graded source strings propagated nowhere; read-path carriage moves tokens, not conventions. Confirmed 09-01 across eight observations, every one obeying a read path: central absorbed go-7 directly and fissioned cen-2 the same run; its QUESTIONS appends carried fission to genetic, tests, map and pattern — each adopted on its next run, the two that did not run for four days adopting the hour they did (relay 5-for-5) — and tests' tst-5 fission arrived through no carriage at all, its own adversarial pass re-deriving the discipline from an in-lane precedent. Three more, 09-02. Negative: five LOG-row flags across four lanes over six days (a stale edge, mutual pairs, stale sibling references, old claim wording — go-12 has them) produced zero uptake, the earliest surviving three runs of the flagged lane; a LOG row is on no lane's read path but central's digest read — the same rule, passive channel. Null: the two subject lanes seeded 09-01 carry no sources at all — nothing yet to grade, so seeding is not evidence either way. Positive, and the first time this lane's theory shaped the charter: §12's feedback loop is built as an active channel — a file in the lane's own directory, read in Orient by contract, answered in LOG by contract, re-scored next review — and rev-4 cites this node as the mechanism it rests on. Consequence: convergence needs an active channel — enforced artifacts (schema plus checker), central's QUESTIONS relay, the review's FEEDBACK loop, or in-lane adversarial re-derivation; passive availability moves nothing. Standing verdicts: go-8's rule fired, answer no; any future grade field is schema-defined, lane-populated, optional-and-empty at migration; health.mjs counts source-string markers only.

nodes.claim: Run cadence is a graph-health dimension no content metric can see: every prior signal is a function of what the graphs say, so a program that stops running reads as maximally healthy — each lane's run recency must be measured alongside content.
nodes.detail: Measured 2026-09-01: zero landings program-wide from 08-29 until that run — the even-date group missed its 08-30 cycle entirely, the odd-date group 08-31, and the odd group's 09-01 slots (09:02–12:02 UTC) had passed landing nothing by the write (~13:00) — the weekly digest due after Sunday 08-30 unwritten. That run itself fired on 09-01, off this lane's even-date schedule. The account side could not say why: all Routines read enabled with no run-outcome record, which dispatcher-bound Routines record none of by contract — so among the artifacts any lane or the digest reads, silence shows only in the branch, and only if measured. Every pre-existing signal is computed from graph content, constant under a stopped program — the gap sat under a green checker until dates were compared by hand. This is go-6's blindness generalized — silence is the recording rate at zero — and it inverts go-2's decay lens: a silent corpus neither rots visibly nor lives. Remedy, same run: health.mjs reports each lane's last LOG.md row date and age, flagging silence past SILENT_DAYS=2 — LOG.md because it is append-only, one row per run, and a nothing-advanced run still logs (§3), where graph.updated moves only on content (or, since 09-02, a recorded re-read) — descriptive, never gating (go-5); re-pacing stays the owner's dial (§11). Limits: the metric trusts each row's leading date; a lane padding rows reads alive (§3's ratchet names that failure); and the flag's availability depends on some lane running — a measurement that vanishes with the program it measures. Cost of the gap: map's and pattern's routed fission questions sat unread, then were acted on in recovery's first hour. Resolved 2026-09-02. The cause reached the tree through central's 09-01 digest notes and LOG row — a dispatcher backlog, drained ~12:53 UTC ('14 → 10 dispatched') — so 'recovery or manual dispatch' resolved to the dispatcher stalling with every Routine healthy: a failure only the branch's timestamps could see. The drain shows in landing times: the odd group landed 13:19–13:29 on 09-01, four lanes in ten minutes; the even group is on schedule 09-02 (08:42, 09:31, 10:32, this run at 11:02; central's 12:02 slot ahead). Silent lanes now: none. Consumers: the 09-01 digest reported the gap independently (its own health run plus the account side; it read this lane's 08-28 summary, one landing before the metric existed) and the review rubric's zero anchor cites this node.

nodes.claim: Edge resolution is necessary, not sufficient: an edge warrants against its target's claim as that claim read when the edge was made, so after a rewrite or fission the edge is current only if its owner re-read it — and until this run nothing in the program measured that.
nodes.detail: Measured 2026-09-02 over 12 graphs, 321 edges. The checker proves every edge target exists; yet 25 edges (8%; 19 cross-graph) are older than their target's last claim change, from git claim-change dates (`updated` moves on detail and edges too and would flag 49). Where rewriting concentrates, edges age: six point at cen-1, rewritten twice, five of them supports edges from genetic, database and this lane still warranted against its pre-fork singular form; central's nine flagged out-edges reach eight targets in five graphs (its own cen-1 among them) rewritten since 08-28 — the lane with the most cross-edges ages fastest.
